scope: Original Mayfair 2010/2013 English 2–4-player base plus applicable unified base clarifications. Exclude expansions, revised-2024 six-player rules and optional Gamble Variant. Unified p2 ignores absent expansion elements.

independence.accessed_material: Only the two authorized rule text extractions, their primary PDFs, original native p1–4 images, and the five current authorized bank files. Repository instruction-file path discovery did not open any QA or other AGENTS content.
independence.method: Full contiguous source/bank reads followed by primary-page visual checks and clause-by-clause source reasoning. Ledger claims were challenged, not treated as proof.

Unified physical p9 Settling Who’s the Boss, complete procedure, narrative, example and diagrams

Original p4/unified p15 Trading for replacement value
Q27_source_limit_interpretation.what_is_determinate: Green replaces at six. Red’s remaining six and Green’s six are current highest across players and reroll immediately; Blue’s three does not initially roll. Resolve current-highest cross-player ties fully before actions or initiating further trades.
Q27_source_limit_interpretation.narrative_and_diagram_check: Both tie narratives say that if two players reroll below another player’s die, the third becomes boss. This describes the competing players and supports the ordinary owner-roll reading, but does not expressly allocate every physical throw or state an exclusive mandatory owner-only rule. The examples use passive wording about both fives being rerolled; diagrams circle the participating colored dice and show outcomes, without depicting or labeling a physical thrower.
Q27_source_limit_interpretation.reorganization_distinction: Original p3 expressly says you reroll your dice and other players reroll theirs; unified p11 expressly says each player rerolls all their dice. Those instructions occur inside Reorganization, so they cannot establish an unstated universal tie-rule mandate.
Q27_source_limit_interpretation.key_claim_truth: The correction’s narrow claim that the supplied free boss-tie rules do not expressly designate a mandatory physical thrower is accurate. It correctly refrains from anyone-may-roll permission and from a mandatory owner-only allocation.
Q27_source_limit_interpretation.strict_benchmark_determination: The retained wording asks who rolls as a gameplay actor. A candid source-limits statement is valid evidence about the books, but does not recover that definite actor. Therefore a fully determinate strict-source gameplay benchmark cannot receive an unqualified PASS while retaining that material asked part as though definitively answered. This finding is a scope/completeness limitation, not an accusation that the corrected source-limits sentence is false.
Q27_source_limit_interpretation.needed_resolution: An applicable authoritative clarification allocating the free tie roller, or an explicit benchmark scope decision that the asked clause tests source limits rather than a definite gameplay person. No person or permission is invented here.

per_question_checks.question: How are starting properties and money assigned, where do the dealt cards go, and how is the End of Game card inserted?

required_fact_checks.fact: Remove End of Game, shuffle, deal two property cards per player.
Mark the two initial lots and take starting money equal to the sum of their printed card money values.
Discard by color/Strip with counts visible.
Divide remaining shuffled deck into four roughly equal stacks; End of Game on top of fourth, other three on top.

background_classification.text: These card values are only used during setup; Q03 asks that limitation explicitly.

per_question_checks.references: Original p2 Setting Up; unified p5
per_question_checks.independent_check: All four asked setup clauses are represented: card preparation/deal, property and initial-money assignment, visible discard destination, and fourth-stack insertion. F replacement is separately asked in Q20.

per_question_checks.question: Who takes the first turn, how does turn order proceed, and what is the normal Draw/Play sequence?

required_fact_checks.fact: Each rolls two dice; highest roller takes player card and first turn.
Pass player card left after each turn.
Draw property card, take its lot, pay all owned lots, pay/score indicated casinos, discard appropriately, then Play actions.

per_question_checks.references: Original p2 Taking Turns/On Every Turn; p3 Ending Step 1
per_question_checks.independent_check: Two-dice highest roller, left succession with player card, acquisition before both payout classes, appropriate discard, then actions are all source-backed. No expansion draw step is imported.

per_question_checks.question: You draw the card for an empty lot. When is it acquired and paid, and do the printed card starting-money values pay again?

required_fact_checks.fact: Place your marker before payouts.
The newly acquired marked lot pays you $1 in the coming lot payout.
Card money values are used only during setup, not drawn-turn income.

background_classification.text: All other marked lots also pay their owners $1, tested by Q02/Q06.

per_question_checks.references: Original p2 Setting Up/Take Over Your Lot/Owned Lots Pay
per_question_checks.independent_check: Acquisition precedes the universal marked-lot payout. Starting-money card values do not recur. Other lots are correctly context rather than an extra response demand.

per_question_checks.question: You draw a lot card for a sprawled tile with an opponent’s 5, although the board prints 2. What happens to the tile and die, and who receives its imminent matching-color money?

required_fact_checks.fact: Tile stays; replace opposing die with your own retaining current value 5, not printed 2.
Takeover precedes payout; you, the drawing player/new owner, receive the imminent matching-color money for the replaced die.

background_classification.text: At current value5 that die yields $5, but Q04 asks who receives the money, not its amount. The die retains value5 as explicitly asked. Per-pip arithmetic is tested directly by Q06/Q24.

per_question_checks.references: Original p2 Take Over Your Lot/Money Paid
per_question_checks.independent_check: Existing opponent die value survives replacement; built tile persists; acquisition precedes matching payout. Amount is not an extra asked clause.

per_question_checks.question: When do same-color tiles form one casino, can they be divided, and is the boss determined by total pips or something else?

required_fact_checks.fact: Edge-connected same-color tiles on same block form a single indivisible casino; diagonal-only contact does not.
Boss is owner of highest individual die, not greatest total pips or most tiles.

background_classification.text: Casino colors do not denote player colors.

per_question_checks.references: Original p1 Casino Tiles/Player Dice; p2 Who Owns What
per_question_checks.independent_check: Edge-connected same-color tiles within a block merge indivisibly; maximum individual die determines boss. Equal-height qualifications belong to the excluded riser mechanics.

per_question_checks.question: A three-tile gold casino contains Red 5 and Blue 3 and 2; Red also owns two marked lots. On a gold payout, how much money and how many points does each receive from these holdings?

required_fact_checks.fact: Red receives $7: $5 die plus $2 lots.
Blue receives $5 from dice.
Red boss receives 3 casino points, Blue no casino points.

per_question_checks.references: Original p2 Owned Lots Pay/Money Paid/Points Earned
per_question_checks.independent_check: The keyed arithmetic is correct: Red money includes two lots, Blue sums both dice, and only boss receives casino points. These are point awards, subject to ordinary track breaks.

per_question_checks.question: How does Pay The Strip differ from a color payout, and what qualifies a casino whose only one tile touches The Strip?

required_fact_checks.fact: Color pays all casinos of that color anywhere.
Strip pays all colors with at least one casino edge adjacent to Strip.
Entire qualifying casino pays money/points for all tiles, not only touching tile.

per_question_checks.references: Original p2 Pay Based on Color/Pay The Strip; unified p8
per_question_checks.independent_check: Color payout is board-wide for that color; Strip qualification is an edge, and its whole casino pays. One touching tile qualifies all constituent tiles.

per_question_checks.question: Which actions may you take in Play, in what order and how often, and may another player perform an action on your turn?

required_fact_checks.fact: Build, sprawl, remodel, reorganize, gamble in any order.
All may repeat except gamble once per own turn; reorganization also limited per die per turn.
No player takes actions on another player’s turn.

background_classification.text: Trading may occur at any time subject to exceptions; tested by Q17/Q27/Q32.

per_question_checks.references: Original p3 Step 2 Play/Reorganize; p4 Trading
per_question_checks.independent_check: The five base actions, arbitrary order, repetition exception, reorganization die limit and prohibition on another player taking actions are supported.

per_question_checks.question: How do you build on your marked lot whose board price is $6 and printed die is 2? State cost, marker and die handling, and tile choice.

required_fact_checks.fact: Pay $6; choose available casino tile color.
Remove/reclaim marker, place tile and your die set to printed board value2.

background_classification.text: The question gives your marked lot. Build ownership eligibility is explicitly tested by Q37, not credited from this scenario given.

per_question_checks.references: Original p3 Build; unified p10 Build
per_question_checks.independent_check: Cost, available color choice, marker reclamation, and board-printed die value are asked and correctly required. Ownership is a given here; Q37 separately tests it.

per_question_checks.question: You boss a gold casino and want to sprawl onto an edge-adjacent empty unowned $9 lot with printed die 3. What do you pay and place, and may you instead sprawl onto an opponent’s marked lot or a merely diagonal lot?

required_fact_checks.fact: Pay $18, place available gold tile with own die 3.
The stated eligible lot is empty/unowned and edge-adjacent; opponent-marked and diagonal-only targets are illegal.
Cannot sprawl without available tile of same color.

background_classification.text: The question already gives that the acting player is the casino boss; no need to restate a given as an extra fact.

per_question_checks.references: Original p3 Sprawl
per_question_checks.independent_check: Double printed cost, same-color available tile and own die at board value are correct. Opponent marker and diagonal adjacency are explicitly ruled out. Boss is a scenario given; Q36 separately tests eligibility.

per_question_checks.question: How does remodeling a two-tile casino work, including eligibility, cost, tile supply, and a merger with a neighboring casino whose highest die beats yours?

required_fact_checks.fact: Must boss casino; remodel all its tiles into one new color with enough available tiles.
Pay $10 ($5 each); replace all tiles with new-color tiles; dice/holdings remain.
Edge-adjacent same-color casinos merge; in the stated case, the neighboring casino’s higher-die owner becomes boss of the merged casino.
Return replaced old-color tiles to their supply.

per_question_checks.references: Original p3 Remodel and example; unified p11
per_question_checks.independent_check: Boss eligibility, entire-casino recoloring, adequate supply, per-tile payment, returned old tiles and merger control are supported. The stated neighboring highest die wins.

per_question_checks.question: May a non-boss with one die reorganize a casino with dice 5, 3 and 2? State who pays how much, which dice roll and who rolls them, and where multiple dice may return.

required_fact_checks.fact: Yes, at least one own die suffices; acting player pays $10 total pips of all dice.
All dice reroll, each owner rolling their own.
Each owner returns dice only to their own original tiles, choosing assignment among those tiles if multiple.

per_question_checks.references: Original p3 Reorganize
per_question_checks.independent_check: Having one die permits a non-boss to pay the total-pip cost. All dice reroll; the sources expressly assign each owner their own reorganization dice and allow reassignment only among that owner’s original tiles.

per_question_checks.question: A die was reorganized earlier this turn and its casino then merges into a larger casino. Can the larger casino be reorganized this turn, and are free boss-tie rerolls prohibited too?

required_fact_checks.fact: No: no die may be reorganized more than once per turn, so any previously reorganized die prevents reorganization of the enlarged casino.
Boss-tie rerolls are free and not subject to reorganization once-per-turn limit.

per_question_checks.references: Original p3 Reorganize; p4 Reroll if Tied; unified p11
per_question_checks.independent_check: One previously reorganized die prevents reorganizing the enlarged casino. The unified clarification expressly separates reorganization limits from unlimited needed free tie rerolls.

per_question_checks.question: After a merger, Red 5 and Blue 5 tie above Green 4. What rerolls, at what cost, and who bosses if both 5s reroll to 3? What if all largest tied dice belong to one player, or only smaller dice tie?

required_fact_checks.fact: Immediately reroll only tied largest dice at no cost.
If both become 3, Green unchanged 4 is boss; do not keep rerolling smaller 3s.
Same-player highest tie requires no reroll; ties below highest require none.
If different players remain tied for current highest, repeat with current highest until one player controls highest.

per_question_checks.references: Original p4 After Each Action Reroll if Tied and diagram
per_question_checks.independent_check: The source example supports immediate free highest-only rerolls and the untouched lower die becoming boss. Same-owner highest ties and subordinate ties do not trigger rolls; reassess current highest after every roll.

per_question_checks.question: You have $18 and gamble at an opponent’s four-tile casino whose boss has $15. What is the maximum bet, who gets the House card, and how many times may you gamble this turn?

required_fact_checks.fact: Maximum $15: minimum of $20 tile cap, own $18 and boss $15.
Gamble once during own turn.
Give the casino boss the House card.

background_classification.text: Casino must be bossed by another player.

per_question_checks.references: Original p4 Gamble
per_question_checks.independent_check: Minimum of casino size limit, gambler bankroll and House bankroll is correct. House card goes to chosen casino’s boss; gamble once per own turn. This does not ask who physically rolls the gambling dice.

per_question_checks.question: For a legal $4 bet against a boss who has $7, resolve every possible two-dice sum group, including the limited doubled payout. Is a winning bettor also losing their stake?

required_fact_checks.fact: 3/4/9/10/11: win $4 from boss and retain/get stake back.
2/12: nominal win $8 but receive only boss’s available $7 and retain/get stake back.
5/6/7/8: lose/pay $4 to boss.

per_question_checks.references: Original p4 Gamble; unified p13
per_question_checks.independent_check: Every sum classification and capped doubled payment is correct, including return/retention of stake. Two dice and a sum are presupposed by the question; the required facts never ask or specify the physical gambling roller.

per_question_checks.question: What may be traded, when may trading occur, how are traded lots and dice transferred, and what cannot be promised or traded?

required_fact_checks.fact: Trade money, lots, casino dice and actions on the active player’s current turn. Trading may occur even off-turn, except no initiated trades during unresolved boss ties or after End of Game is drawn.
Replace lot marker with recipient marker; replace die with recipient die at same current pip value, not board value.
No points or casino tiles; no promises of future-turn actions/exchanges/transfers.
No actions on another player’s turn.

per_question_checks.references: Original p4 Trading; unified physicalp9 Settling Who’s the Boss, physicalp15 Trading, physicalp16 Winning.
per_question_checks.independent_check: Broad what/when/transfer/prohibition clauses justify the listed assets and timing exceptions. Only active player may perform traded actions; future-turn promises are forbidden. Base-only assets correctly exclude expansion cards.

per_question_checks.question: Starting at score 8, where do single casino awards of 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 points leave you? Can two separate one-tile casinos combine their awards, and in what order are different casinos scored?

required_fact_checks.fact: 1 leaves 8; 2 or 3 reaches 10; 4 or 5 reaches 12.
Insufficient excess at a break is lost; cannot pool separate casino awards.
Score each casino independently smallest to largest, player chooses equal-size order; two single-tile awards leave 8.

per_question_checks.references: Original p2 Scoring; p3 scoring example and multiple casinos
per_question_checks.independent_check: All five award outcomes, separate-casino handling, lost insufficient excess and smallest-to-largest order with choice on ties are directly supported.

per_question_checks.question: What happens when the End of Game card is drawn, including remaining actions, final payouts, winner and tied score? Is there an immediate alternative win condition?

required_fact_checks.fact: Game ends immediately; no subsequent Play actions.
Final payout all owned lots and casinos touching Strip, with ordinary money and scoring rules.
Most points wins; tied most points breaks by most money.
90+ points wins immediately in base game.

per_question_checks.references: Original p4 Winning; unified p16
per_question_checks.independent_check: Immediate end, final owned-lot plus Strip payout, points/money winner comparison and immediate 90+ base win are correct. Expansion end-point modifications are excluded.

per_question_checks.question: In two-player play, what happens to F cards drawn during setup and during a turn? May anyone build on F, and can a turn pay more than once before actions?

required_fact_checks.fact: No building on F block.
Discard and replace an F card drawn during setup; use accepted A–E starting cards.
During turn do not mark F; pay owned lots and indicated casinos/points, discard then repeat Draw until A–E card resolved.
Each such draw pays, so multiple payouts occur in one turn before Play.

background_classification.text: An End of Game draw interrupts immediately; Q19 and Q32 test end priority.
The accepted starting cards determine initial properties and money; that normal setup resource calculation is asked by Q01, not an extra Q20 requirement.

per_question_checks.references: Original p4 2-Player Rules/Winning; unified p16 2-Player Rules
per_question_checks.independent_check: Applicable unified clarification expressly replaces F setup cards. During turns each F card still pays and is discarded before another draw, without marking F; no building on F. End trigger retains priority.

per_question_checks.question: All nine gold tiles are on the board. Can you build another gold tile using the spare tenth tile, sprawl a gold casino, or remodel a three-tile casino to gold? May you build a different available color?

required_fact_checks.fact: The tenth is a replacement, not a tenth usable tile.
Cannot build gold, sprawl gold or remodel to gold without sufficient available tiles.
Yes, a different available color may be built on an owned lot.

background_classification.text: Normal build cost applies; this question does not give a price or ask a monetary calculation.

per_question_checks.references: Original p1 Casino Tiles; p3 Available Tiles/Build/Sprawl/Remodel
per_question_checks.independent_check: Ninth-tile exhaustion applies to all three placement actions; spare tenth is a replacement. An available different color remains legal for Build on an owned lot.

per_question_checks.question: All twelve of your dice are on the board when you build, sprawl or inherit a sprawled tile. How do you place the required die, what happens to the vacated tile and its scoring, and what if it was the casino’s only die?

required_fact_checks.fact: Remove one of your existing ownership dice and place it on the new tile at the value required by the placement.
Vacated tile remains ownerless but counts for casino points.
If no dice remain in a casino it has no owner/boss.

per_question_checks.references: Original p3 Available Dice; unified p6 Available Dice
per_question_checks.independent_check: Mandatory reuse of an existing own ownership die leaves its old tile present and ownerless but countable for points. A wholly dice-free casino has no boss. Placement value comes from the placement-specific rule.

per_question_checks.question: A property draw claims a sprawled casino tile with no die; the board prints 2, while the die removed from it used to be 5. What die do you place, does the tile change, and when does its matching casino pay?

required_fact_checks.fact: Place own die at printed board value 2; former removed value 5 is not retained.
Casino tile remains; acquisition precedes matching casino payment.

background_classification.text: The new value2 die pays its owner $2 on that payout, but income amount is not asked here.

per_question_checks.references: Original p2 Take Over Your Lot/Money Paid; unified p7
per_question_checks.independent_check: A vacant die hole uses printed board value, not a removed historical die. Tile persists and takeover occurs before payment.

per_question_checks.question: You draw the card for your own sprawled tile, whose die is now 6 although the board prints 2. Does ownership or value change, and what does that die earn if its casino pays?

required_fact_checks.fact: Leave your existing die unchanged at 6.
Matching payout pays you $6 for that die.

per_question_checks.references: Unified p7 Step 2; original p2 Money Paid
per_question_checks.independent_check: Unified instruction expressly leaves the drawing player’s own die alone. The current six pays six when that casino pays.

per_question_checks.question: All ten of your markers are on lots and you acquire another empty lot. How is ownership marked, what happens to the vacated lot, and which of the two lots receives the coming owned-lot payout?

required_fact_checks.fact: Move one existing marker to newly gained lot.
You no longer own vacated lot; it does not pay you lot income.
New marked lot pays you $1 in upcoming payout.

per_question_checks.references: Unified p6 Available Player Markers; original p2 Draw/Owned Lots Pay
per_question_checks.independent_check: Exhausted markers must be moved to the new lot. Vacated lot loses ownership, so only the newly marked of those two lots pays its owner.

per_question_checks.question: May a player conceal money or piece counts, forbid inspection of a discard pile, or deny a bank payout because the physical bank is empty?

required_fact_checks.fact: Money, piece counts and discarded cards are public; anyone may inspect discards.
Bank money unlimited; physical bank exhaustion does not cancel a payout.

per_question_checks.references: Original p1 Money; unified p6 Your Resources/Available Money
per_question_checks.independent_check: No-hidden-information, discard inspection and unlimited-bank clarifications are applicable without expansions.

per_question_checks.question: A casino has two Red 6s and a Blue 3. During a trade one Red 6 is replaced by Green’s die. What value does Green’s die have, must anything reroll before further trades or actions, and who rolls?

required_fact_checks.fact: Green’s replacement die retains value6.
The remaining Red6 and new Green6 are tied for highest across different players; reroll those two dice immediately, not Blue3 initially.
Finish resolving any current-highest cross-player ties before actions or initiating more trades; after each reroll reassess the current highest dice and stop when one player owns the highest value.

For physical roller identity, the supplied free boss-tie rules do not explicitly designate who throws each die. They specify which owners’ dice participate. The each-player-rolls-own instruction is expressly part of paid Reorganization, not a stated universal free-tie actor rule. Do not invent a mandatory owner-only allocation or an any-person permission.

background_classification.text: Boss-tie rerolls are free; Q14 explicitly asks cost, Q27 does not.

per_question_checks.references: Original p4 Trading/Reroll if Tied and its narrative/example; unified physicalp9 Settling Who’s the Boss; originalp3/unifiedp11 Reorganize for the expressly local roller instruction.
per_question_checks.independent_check: Replacement value, cross-player tie membership and immediate uninterrupted resolution are supported. The key accurately identifies a source limitation on a mandatory physical roller. It does not supply a definite physical gameplay actor for the retained final clause; see the separate source-limit determination.

per_question_checks.question: You draw a card and replace one of Red’s tied highest 5s in a casino with your own 5; another Red 5 remains. Is the boss tie postponed until after payment or Play, and does this reroll count as a paid reorganization?

required_fact_checks.fact: Resolve cross-player highest tie immediately on takeover before casino payouts, not postponed to Play.
Reroll only current highest dice free; this is not paid reorganization and does not use its limit.

per_question_checks.references: Unified p7 Step 2/p9 Settling Who’s the Boss; p11 Reorganize
per_question_checks.independent_check: The unified whenever-tied rule expressly includes takeover, so resolve before payout, with no reorganization cost or consumed reorganization allowance.

per_question_checks.question: May you reorganize a casino where you alone own all dice, or one where you own none? Does reorganizing only one of your dice avoid paying for the opponents’ pips?

required_fact_checks.fact: Sole owner may reorganize; no-own-die casino may not.
Reorganization always rerolls every die and costs all pips, including opponents, not just selected own dice.

per_question_checks.references: Original p3 Reorganize; unified p11
per_question_checks.independent_check: At least one own die is necessary, sole ownership is sufficient, and no selective-dice/partial-pip reorganization exists.

per_question_checks.question: All twelve of your ownership dice are on casino tiles. Must you remove a tile’s die just to gamble, and may you gamble at your own casino if no opponent bosses any casino?

required_fact_checks.fact: Any dice may be used to gamble; no ownership placement or removal required for the gambling roll.
Cannot gamble at own casino; if no opponent bosses a casino there is no legal gambling action.

per_question_checks.references: Unified p6 Available Dice; p13 Gamble
per_question_checks.independent_check: Any dice may be borrowed for gambling without moving ownership dice. Gambling requires another player as boss; absent an eligible casino there is no gambling action. Any-dice supply permission does not state who throws them.

per_question_checks.question: On your turn you trade for an opponent’s die so that you can reorganize their casino, then promise to pay them for a sprawl only if the reorganization gives you control. If the reroll does not make you boss so the agreed sprawl cannot happen, do the subsequent steps of the trade proceed? Could the opponent instead perform the sprawl on your turn?

required_fact_checks.fact: When an element of trade is prevented, subsequent steps do not occur.
Opponent cannot take action on your turn.

background_classification.text: The scenario itself gives that failed boss control means the agreed sprawl cannot happen. This is not an independently asked rule in Q31; Q36 now explicitly tests boss-only sprawl eligibility.

per_question_checks.references: Unified p15 Trading; original p3 Sprawl/p4 Trading
per_question_checks.independent_check: The source expressly stops subsequent trade steps when an element is prevented. Opponent cannot perform a sprawl on active player’s turn. Active-player same-turn intended sprawl is the reasonable scenario reading; no future-turn promise is authorized.

per_question_checks.question: The End of Game card has just been drawn. Before the final payout, may players initiate a last-minute trade of money or a casino die, perhaps to change who wins a tied score?

required_fact_checks.fact: No: End of Game draw immediately ends play, so players cannot initiate a money/die trade before final payouts.

background_classification.text: Final lots and Strip payouts, score/money win comparison are already asked by Q19; they are not additional requirements for this trade-priority question.

per_question_checks.references: Original p4 Winning; unified physical p16 Winning, first paragraph (no actions or initiated trades on End of Game draw).
per_question_checks.independent_check: Unified Winning expressly bars initiated trades once end card is drawn, before final payouts. Existing payout/winner rules are background rather than extra demands.

per_question_checks.question: During setup, which pieces does each player take, and where is each player’s scoring chip placed before the first turn?

required_fact_checks.fact: Each player takes an action card and the scoring chip, markers and dice of one player color. Place every player’s scoring chip on 0 on the scoring track.

per_question_checks.references: Original p2 Setting Up, first and third paragraphs; unified physical p5 Setting Up.
per_question_checks.independent_check: All named player pieces of a single color and score chip on zero are source-backed and directly asked.

per_question_checks.question: Must a trade be between exactly two players, or may three players participate in one agreed trade of their money, lots and casino dice?

required_fact_checks.fact: Any number of players may be involved in a trade, so a three-player trade is permitted, subject to the ordinary restrictions on traded assets and timing.

per_question_checks.references: Unified physical p15 At Any Time: Trading, first paragraph: any number of players may be involved. Original p4 Trading supplies base assets and restrictions.
per_question_checks.independent_check: Any number of participants may agree to one trade. Ordinary asset/timing restrictions remain context, not a demand to restate every trading rule.

per_question_checks.question: Besides taking their own components, what banking role must the group assign during setup?

required_fact_checks.fact: Choose a player to be the Banker.

per_question_checks.references: Original p2 Setting Up, second paragraph; unified physical p5 Setting Up.
per_question_checks.independent_check: Choosing one player as Banker is an express setup instruction.

per_question_checks.question: You have a die in a casino, but another player is its boss. May you sprawl that casino during your own turn?

required_fact_checks.fact: No. Only the boss may sprawl a casino; merely owning a die is insufficient.

per_question_checks.references: Original p3 Action–Sprawl; unified physicalp10 Sprawl.
per_question_checks.independent_check: Sprawl eligibility belongs only to the boss, not merely any dice owner.

per_question_checks.question: May you use Build on an empty unowned lot or another player’s marked lot, or must the target be a lot you own?

required_fact_checks.fact: Build may be used only on a lot you own. An unowned lot or another player’s marked lot is not a legal Build target.

per_question_checks.references: Original p3 Action–Build; unified physicalp10 Build.
per_question_checks.independent_check: Build requires the acting player’s own lot; neither unowned nor opponent-owned targets qualify.

per_question_checks.question: Next to a casino you boss is an edge-adjacent, built casino tile of another color with no die. Is it a legal Sprawl target because it is unowned, or must the target be an empty lot?

required_fact_checks.fact: No. A built casino tile remains on the board even without a die; it is a casino space, not an empty lot. Sprawl requires an empty, unowned lot, so you cannot sprawl onto or replace this tile.

per_question_checks.references: Original p2 Who Owns What; p3 Available Dice and Action–Sprawl; unified physicalp6 Available Dice and p10 Sprawl.
per_question_checks.independent_check: A built tile with no die remains an occupied casino space, not an empty lot, and cannot be sprawled over. The color and boss/adjacency givens add no unasked requirements.

--- Page 1 ---
1
Las Vegas, 1941. Stretching before you is Highway 
91, soon to be known as the Las Vegas Strip. In this 
desert landscape you see the future home of the most 
fabulous hotels and casinos in the world. Over the next 
few decades, you and your fellow developers will build 
the Las Vegas Strip from the ground up, vying to become 
the new Lords of Vegas.
Summary
In Lords of Vegas, you are a Las Vegas developer and 
casino boss. You build casinos, trade properties, gamble 
in other players’ casinos, and improve the casinos you 
manage. You are paid points and money for controlling 
the best casinos and in the end, the player with the most 
points wins.
Objective
You win the game by accumulating the most points. 
You are paid points when your casinos’ colors are 
drawn—larger casinos are worth more points. Casinos 
also pay money, which you can spend to manage your 
properties. Your basic strategy is to build and control the 
largest and best casinos.
COMPONENTS
The Board: The board represents an abstract section of 
Las Vegas Boulevard (“The Strip”). Each square on the 
board begins as an unowned space called a “lot.” You 
own each lot that contains 1 of your translucent markers. 
You also own each lot that contains a casino tile with 1 of 
your dice (your owned property). The board also has a  
scoring track, a wager space, and discard spaces  
for played cards.
Casino Tiles: These square pieces 
represent individual casinos, or 
sections of larger casinos. There are 
9 tiles* in each of 5 colors (aqua, 
brown, gold, purple, and silver). The 
casino colors do NOT correspond to 
player colors. When 2 or more tiles of 
the same color make up a contiguous 
group on the same block, they are treated as a single 
large casino that cannot be subdivided. The square hole 
in the center of the tile is designed 
to hold 1 player die.
*The 10th tile can be used as a 
replacement.
Player Dice: Each player has  
12 dice, representing 
influence in casinos. The 
four player colors are blue, 
green, red, and yellow. 
When you own a tile, you 
mark it with a die. The value 
on the die indicates how 
much influence you have in 
that space. The single die 
with the largest value in a given 
casino designates the boss of  
that casino.
Player Markers: Each player has 
10 markers. These are used to 
mark owned spaces. 
When you own a 
space on the board, 
place a marker on it 
until you build a casino 
tile there, or until you trade or sell 
that space to another player.
Scoring Chips: Your scoring chip begins 
on space “0” on the scoring track, and 
records your point total as you are paid 
points.  
Note that the scoring track has numeric 
jumps that make it harder to acquire points at  
higher levels.
Money: All values in this game are 
described in dollars ($1, $5, $10, $20) 
but represent millions of dollars ($1M, 
$5M, $10M, $20M). You cannot hide 
how much money you have.
Property Cards: There are  
49 property cards in the deck. Each card 
corresponds to a single space on the 
board. One of these cards is the End of 
Game card, which is a property card that 
also determines when the game ends.
Player Card: You pass this card around 
to designate whose turn it is.
House Card: This card is given to 
the house when a player gambles, 
and shows the winning rolls.
Action Cards: Each of these 4 
cards summarize the actions you 
may take during your turn. 
™
A game for 2-4 players by James Ernest & Mike Selinker


--- Page 2 ---
2
Pay Based on Color: When a card with a single color is 
drawn, casinos of that color pay points and money—
everywhere on the board.
Pay The Strip: When 1 of the 4 cards that Pay The Strip 
is drawn, each casino with at least 1 edge adjacent to 
The Strip pays points and money—rather than paying 
based upon a single color. 
Money Paid
When a casino pays money, you are paid $1 for each 
pip on each of your dice in the casino. For example, a red 
5 die pays $5 to the red player.
Points Earned
When a casino earns points, the casino’s boss is paid 
1 point for each tile in that casino. Record your points by 
moving your chip along the scoring track.
Example: It is the Yellow player’s turn. He draws a gold 
card, D8, and marks D8 with one of his markers. The two 
owned lots shown pay money: $1 for Green and $1 for 
Yellow. Because a gold card was drawn, the gold casinos 
pay (everywhere on the board). The Yellow player is paid 
$6 and 1 point for his 1-tile gold casino in the lower right. 
The brown and purple casinos pay no money or points. 
Green is the boss of the 3-tile gold casino, so Green is 
paid 3 points. The dice in that casino pay $2 to Blue, and 
$6 to Green. 
Example: The 1-tile brown casino and the 3-tile gold 
casino both touch The Strip, but the 1-tile purple casino 
and the 1-tile

gold casino do not.
WHO OWNS WHAT
A lot is a space that does not contain a tile. When you 
draw the card that corresponds to a lot, you place  
1 of your markers on that lot—you own that lot. 
When you pay the build cost for a lot you own, you 
place a tile and 1 of your dice on it­—the lot becomes a 
casino, or part of an existing casino. You own that die, 
which represents part of your influence in that casino. 
A casino is a group of 1 or more contiguous tiles of the 
same color—each tile must have at least 1 edge adjacent 
to the edge of another tile. These tiles must be treated as 
1 large casino that cannot be subdivided. Once built, your 
casino is no longer treated as a lot. 
The boss of a casino is the player that owns the 
largest valued die in that casino.
TAKING TURNS
At the start of the game, each player rolls 2 dice. The 
highest roller takes the player card and begins the first 
turn. Each turn represents roughly a year of activity, 
during which certain players and development companies 
prosper. When a player’s turn ends, the next player to the 
left takes the player card and starts a turn. This continues 
until the End of Game card is drawn. 
ON EVERY TURN
Your turn has 2 steps: “Draw” and “Play.”
Step 1: DRAW
To start your turn, draw a new card. Next, take over the 
lot specified on your card. Then all owned lots pay money, 
and the casinos specified by the card pay points and 
money. 
Take Over Your Lot
If the lot specified on your card is empty, place  
1 of your player markers on the lot—you now own it. 
If the lot already has a tile with another player’s die on 
it (due to “sprawling,” see page 3), replace the die on the 
tile with 1 of your dice—keeping the same pip value. If 
the tile has no die, place your die so that the pip value 
matches the die printed on the board.
Owned Lots Pay
Each lot with a player marker on it pays that player $1, 
no matter what card is drawn. 
Casinos Pay
Each turn, the development company specified by the 
card drawn pays money and points.
Most cards specify payment by all casinos matching a 
single color, but 4 cards (including the End of Game card) 
“Pay The Strip.”
SETTING UP
You and the other players each take an action card and 
the scoring chip, markers, and dice of 1 color. 
Choose a player to be the Banker.
Put the scoring chip for each player on the “0” space of 
the scoring track.
Remove the “End of Game” card from the property 
cards and shuffle the remaining cards. Deal 2 cards to 
each player. 
⚀ Put one of your markers on each of the lots (spaces) 
specified by your 2 cards.
⚁ Draw out money from the bank equal to the sum of 
the 2 values shown on your cards. For example, if 
your 2 cards have values of $4 and $7, you start with 
$11. These values 
are only used during 
setup.
⚂ Discard your 2 cards 
by placing them on 
the colored discard 
spaces on the edge 
of the board. It is 
important to see how 
many of each color 
have been drawn, so 
these discard piles 
should be arranged 
so they can be easily 
counted. There are  
9 cards in each color, 
plus 4 cards that pay  
The Strip.
Insert the End of Game card into the shuffled deck 
as follows. Divide the deck into 4 roughly equal stacks, 
and place the End of Game card on top of the 4th stack. 
Then place the other 3 stacks on top, place the draw pile 
beside the board, and you’re ready to begin.
Scoring
You record the points you receive from each casino 
that you are the boss of—advance your scoring chip from 
space to space on the scoring track. Some of the spaces 
require more than 1 point to advance into. This is called 
a “break.” 
To move your scoring chip past a break, you must 
record enough points to satisfy the points required for the 
space past the break. If you do not have enough points, 
your chip stops on the space preceding the break and 
you lose the excess points.

3
Action – Remodel
When you take the remodel action, you change the 
color of the tiles of a casino where you are the boss:
⚀ Choose a new color with enough available tiles to 
replace all of the casino’s tiles. 
⚁ Pay $5 for each tile in the casino.
⚂ Exchange each of the casino’s tiles with a new tile of 
the chosen color.
Example: The Red player decides to remodel his gold 
casino, changing to brown. The cost for this remodel is 
$10, $5 per tile. This merges it with the smaller brown 
casino where Yellow is the boss. Yellow’s 5 die is larger 
than Red’s 3 die—Yellow is the boss of the new casino. 
Action – Build
When you take the build action, you place a new tile on 
any lot that you own:
⚀ Remove your player marker.
⚁ Choose a casino tile. 
⚂ Pay the amount specified on that lot.
⚃ Place the tile. In that tile, place one of your dic

e turned 
so that the lot’s die value is face up. 
Example: Red has a marker on space A2 and can build 
a casino there for $6. He chooses to build a gold tile, and 
he places a die in that tile with a value of 2 facing up (as 
specified on space A2).
Example: If your scoring chip is on the 8-space on the 
scoring track and a casino pays you only 1 point, your 
chip does not advance to the 10-space. If you are paid 2 
or 3 points, your chip advances to the 10-space. If you are 
paid 4 or 5 points, your chip advances to the 12-space.
Action – Sprawl
When you take the sprawl action, you expand a casino 
where you are the boss:
⚀ Pay twice the amount specified on that lot.
⚁ Place a tile of the same color as the sprawling casino 
on any empty, unowned lot with an edge adjacent 
to the sprawling casino. If a tile of that color isn’t 
available, you cannot sprawl.
⚂ In that tile, place one of your dice turned so that the 
lot’s die value is face up. 
Example: Red is sprawling from A2 into A5. He can 
sprawl here because no one owns A5, but he can’t 
expand into A3 because that space is owned by Yellow. 
The new tile must be gold because the original casino  
is gold, and the cost is $18, twice the normal build  
cost of A5.
Strategy: Sprawling can be risky, because the card 
corresponding to the sprawl lot is still in the deck.  
Another player who draws such a card immediately 
replaces the die in that lot with a die of his own  
(see “Take Over Your Lot” on page 2). 
When you are paid points for multiple casinos on 
the same turn, you must record each casino’s points 
individually, starting with the smallest and proceeding 
to the largest (your choice on ties). So, even if several 
casinos of 1 tile each pay you on the same turn, your 
scoing chip still cannot move from the 8-space to the 
10-space.
Ending Step 1
When Step 1 is over, discard your card into the 
appropriate discard pile, and move on to Step 2.
Step 2: PLAY
During Step 2 of your turn, you may perform these 
actions to manage your holdings. These actions are: 
build, sprawl, remodel, reorganize, and gamble. You may 
perform any of these actions in any order, and all of the 
actions other than gamble may be performed multiple 
times. The actions are detailed below, and they are 
summarized on your action card.
Note: You may also trade with other players at any time 
(see page 4).
Available Tiles: If all of the tiles of a given color are 
already on the board, you may not place a tile of that 
color when you build, sprawl, or remodel.
Available Dice: If all of your dice are already on the 
board and you build or sprawl a new tile or inherit 
a sprawled tile, you must remove one of your dice 
and place it in the tile. The resulting tile without a die 
remains on the board. No one owns a tile without a die, 
though it still counts for points in the casino. Note that 
you can trade to free up a die.
Strategy: You can use a remodel to change the likelihood 
of your casino’s color being drawn. You can remodel to 
merge several small casinos that you control into one 
larger one, or to join your casino with a neighbor’s casino. 
Such a “hostile takeover” can be a handy way to become 
the boss of someone else’s property.
Action – Reorganize
When you take the reorganize (re-org) action, you 
force a reroll of all of the dice (not just some of the dice) 
in a casino in which you have at least 1 die. You do not 
have to be the casino’s boss to reorganize a casino. To 
reorganize a casino:
⚀ Pay $1 for each pip on each die in the casino.
⚁ Reroll all the dice in the casino (you reroll your  
dice, other players reroll theirs). You may reorganize 
multiple casinos during your turn, but no die may be  
reorganized more than once in a turn, even if that  
die’s tile becomes part of a larger casino.
⚂ Return the rerolled dice to the original tiles they came 
from. If you return multiple dice, you decide which of 
your original tiles these dice are returned to. 
Note: To keep track of your tiles involved in a re-org, you 
can temporarily put 1 of your markers on each of them. 
Strategy: A reorganization represents a shake-up among 
the influential people in the casino, and it can have 
dramatic effects on the balance of power.
Because some tiles may have been acquired by 
sprawling, proper replacement of dice can be critical after 
a re-org to protect your high rolls from a takeover. 
One common reorganization trick is to build a 
1-tile casino with a starting die value of 1 or 2. Then 
immediately reorganize it at a very low cost, hoping to get 
a higher value.

At Any Time: Trading
You and the other players may trade at any time, even 
when it is not your turn. However, there are restrictions 
on what you may trade. 
You may trade any combination of money, lots, dice in 
casinos, actions (your turn only). 
Example: You may trade a die for a lot. You may trade a 
die for money. You may trade an action you perform this 
turn for money. You may trade a lot and a die for 2 dice.
When you trade a lot, replace your marker on the lot 
with a marker belonging to the player you are trading 
with. When you trade a die, replace your die with a die 
belonging to the player you are trading with. The new 
die has the same value as the die it is replacing, not the 
value marked on the space.
You may not trade points or casino tiles. You may not 
trade promises of actions, exchanges, and/or transfers to 
be performed on future turns. No player may ever take an 
action on another player’s turn.
WINNING
As soon as anyone draws the “End of Game” card, the 
game ends immediately. Make a final payout for “The 
Strip” and all owned lots. If you have the most points after 
this final payout, you win. If there is a tie for most points, 
the tied player with the most money wins.
You can also win immediately if you have 90+ points. 
As far as we know, this has never happened. But, nothing 
is impossible in Las Vegas!	
2-PLAYER RULES
In a 2-player game, you can’t build on F block. When 
you draw a card specifying an F lot (i.e., F1, F2, etc.),  
do not place a marker. Pay for owned lots, pay for 
casinos, and discard the F lot card into the appropriate 
discard pile. Then, repeat Step 1 until you draw and 
resolve a card from an A, B, C, D, or E lot.
So,casinos and owned lots can pay multiple times 
during a single turn­. You keep drawing and paying until 
you get a card specifying A, B, C, D, or E.  
After Each Action:  
Reroll if Tied	
After you take each action, check each casino to see 
if 2 or more players have dice in that casino that are tied 
for largest value. In this case, that casino has multiple 
bosses that are tied. So, all of the dice with the largest 
value must be immediately rerolled.
These rerolls cost nothing. Only the tied largest 
valued dice are rerolled. If still tied for largest value after 
rerolling, reroll the current largest valued dice. Continue 
rerolling until there is only 1 die with the largest value.
If all of the  
tied dice belong 
to the same 
player, no reroll 
takes place.  
If the values of 
the tied dice  
are not the 
largest in the 
casino, no reroll 
takes place.
This power 
struggle can 
sometimes 
have disastrous 
results for the 
players who are 
tied for the boss 
position. If two 
players reroll to 
a number below 
that of another 
player’s die, that 
third player will become the boss.
Example: The Green player is the boss of a 2-tile gold 
casino. Red is the boss of a 3-tile brown casino. Green’s 
dice are 4 & 5; Red has a 5 & 2, and Yellow has a 2. Green 
remodels his gold casino to brown. He is tied with Red for 
control of this new 5-tile casino. Both 5’s are rerolled—each 
gets a 3. Now Green’s 4 is the largest die, so Green is the 
boss and no more rerolls are required.
Example: In the previous example, the Red player 
remodeled his casino in A2 and A5 to match Yellow’s 
brown casino in A3. He now reorganizes the new 3-tile 
casino for a cost of $10 (there are 10 total pips in the 
casino). As a result of this reroll, Red becomes the boss 
of the casino because the Red 5 is now the largest die. 
If the reroll had not gone Red’s way, he could not have 
made another reorganization of the same casino on the 
same turn.
Action – Gamble
You can only take the gamble action once during your 
turn. When you take the gamble action, you bet at a 
casino where another player is the boss. 
⚀ Give another player the 
House card. Choose 1 of his 
or her casinos. 
⚁ Bet up to $5 for each tile in 
that casino. You cannot bet 
more money than you have, 
and you cannot bet more money than that casino has. 
Example: Red chooses a 4-tile casino, and wants to 
bet $20.  However, Blue (the casino’s owner) only has 
$15, so the most Red can bet is $15.
⚂ Roll 2 dice and add the results. If your roll is 3, 4, 9, 
10, or 11, you win, and the casino’s boss pays you an 
amount equal to your bet. If your roll is 2 or 12, the 
boss must pay yo

u twice what you bet! (If the boss 
does not have enough money to fully pay off his portion 
of your bet, you only get the money he does have.) But 
if your roll is 5, 6, 7, or 8, you lose and pay the boss an 
amount equal to your bet. 
Strategy: This bet is the field bet from craps, with a 
house advantage of 5.6%. You usually take this action 
when you need just a little more money for your turn, but 
you can do it for any reason.
Example: Red is the boss of a 3-tile casino. On Yellow’s 
turn, he goes to Red’s casino and wagers $4 (maximum  
is $15). Yellow rolls a 3, and wins $4 from Red.
Gamble Variant
If all players agree, you can use the following variant:
Before the gambler rolls, the boss of the casino taking 
the bet may opt to “lay off” half of the bet to the bank. 
After the roll, If the gambler wins, the casino boss only 
pays half (round down) and the bank pays the rest. 
Of course, if the gambler loses, the casino boss only 
receives half (round down) and the bank gets the rest.

A lot is a space that does not contain a tile.

In a 2-player game, you can’t build on F block. 
When you draw a card specifying an F lot (i.e., 
F1, F2, etc.), do not place a marker. Pay owned 
lots and casinos, score casinos, activate any 
needed card effects, and discard the F lot card 
into the appropriate property slot. Then, draw a 
new property card, repeating this sequence until 
you draw a card from an A, B, C, D, or E lot. If 
this occurs during setup, discard the card and 
draw a replacement.

times during a single turn. You keep drawing 
and paying until you get a card specifying A, B,
